item.title: Victoria Debt Deal Faces Opposition From HSBC Bank
item.description: UK carpet maker Victoria Plc.’s bid to restructure its balance sheet is facing resistance from HSBC Holdings Plc, a holder of the company’s bonds.

item.title: Tether’s Three-Way Crypto Deal Is Called Off, Mallers Steps Down
item.description: A proposed merger of three crypto firms has been scrapped, with one of their leaders stepping down and another consolidating power across the Tether-backed franchise.

item.title: China’s Double Moonshot Moment in the AI Tech Race
item.description: China is closing the technology gap on both AI models and the chips that make them possible

item.title: Trump and Canada tariff threat
item.description: The move would hit about $20 billion worth of Canadian imports to the US

item.title: Data Centers on Track to Suck Up a Fifth of US Power Use by 2035
item.description: Data centers in the US will account for about 20% of the nation’s electricity consumption in 2035, up from 5.9% today, according to BloombergNEF.

item.title: IEA Warns Mideast Hostilities Are Increasing Oil Supply Concerns
item.description: The International Energy Agency said it’s “closely monitoring the situation in oil markets” as escalating hostilities in the Middle East increase the concerns over security of supplies.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Stop Piping Oil to Black Sea After Tanker Attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to stop piping crude to a port on Russia’s Black Sea coast after a spate of attacks on tankers that’s jeopardizing the landlocked Asian country’s ability to produce oil.

item.title: Carlyle in Talks to Hand ESG Consulting Firm Over to Bridgepoint
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. is in talks to hand the keys of sustainability consultancy Anthesis Group over to its private credit lender Bridgepoint Group Plc, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: US-Based Axiom Seeks Hong Kong IPO to Tap China’s Biotech Boom
item.description: Axiom Biosciences is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, a rare move for an American biotechnology firm, and one that would help it tap China’s booming clinical development capabilities.

item.title: Emerging Market Assets Rally on China Tech Support, Iran Talks
item.description: Emerging market stocks rebounded after three days of losses after China mounted a state-sponsored rescue program for its tech shares.

item.title: Dating Apps Face Scam Challenge of AI-Powered ‘Chatfishing’
item.description: Dating-app companies won’t touch the problem, or don’t know how.

item.title: Singapore Leads Record Foreign Investments in Southeast Asia
item.description: Southeast Asia is a “strategic winner” from supply chain shifts and capital reallocation, highlighting the region’s resilience, according to United Overseas Bank Ltd..

item.title: The New Insider Traders Lurking on Prediction Markets
item.description: Sites like Polymarket can be rewarding for traders with inside info. There are different ways to get it.

item.title: World Hunger Eases for Third Year But War and El Niño Pose Risks
item.description: Global hunger is in retreat, but the Middle East conflict and El Niño weather phenomenon pose new threats, according to United Nations agencies.

item.title: The Great British Takeover Tops $60 Billion After Mitie Deal
item.description: The UK stock market is losing the equivalent of more than $2 billion a week to takeovers of London-listed companies, with Mitie Group Plc the latest name to be snapped up.

item.title: Danantara Hires Banks for Planned Second Dollar Bond Sale
item.description: Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara has mandated banks to sound out investor demand for a potential sale of long-dated dollar bonds, weeks after completing its first offshore debt offering.

item.title: Zalando Avoids Fine as German Regulator Ends Disclosure Probe
item.description: Germany’s financial regulator concluded a review into Zalando SE over a missing disclosure in its annual report without imposing a fine.

item.title: Millikin University Sweetens Bond Deal by Adding 600-Bed Student Apartments
item.description: A private college in Illinois is sweetening its upcoming bond deal by adding a student apartment complex to increase investor protections.

item.title: BlackRock-MGX Consortium Eyes $5 Billion Aligned Data Centers Expansion
item.description: A consortium including BlackRock Inc.’s Global Infrastructure Partners and Abu Dhabi’s MGX plans to invest $5 billion to boost growth at Aligned Data Centers.

item.title: Germany’s Investor Outlook Reaches Five-Month High After Reforms
item.description: German investor optimism rose to the highest level in five months, a sign of hope that Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s economic reforms will spur growth.

item.title: TSMC to Hike Chip Prices By Up to 10% in 2027, Nikkei Says
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. has held discussions with clients about chipmaking price increases of as much as 10% in 2027 to cover the rising cost of manufacturing, the Nikkei reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: HSBC’s Kettner Sees Risk of Pullback in Stocks Before Midterms
item.description: Equity investors should look to reduce some exposure after this earnings season, according to HSBC Holdings Plc’s Max Kettner, who warns that stretched sentiment, a fading fiscal impulse, and US midterm election uncertainty could trigger a pullback.

item.title: BlackRock, Hillhouse, Temasek Said Set to Back Innolight Listing
item.description: BlackRock Inc., Hillhouse Investment and Temasek Holdings Pte are set to be among cornerstone investors in the potential $8 billion listing by Zhongji Innolight Co. in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Euro-Zone Banks Further Tighten Companies’ Credit Standards
item.description: Euro-zone banks tightened corporate credit standards further as they see higher risks due to geopolitical events including the Iran war.

item.title: Gilts Climb as Investors Await More Policy Details From Burnham
item.description: UK government bonds posted small moves as investors awaited fresh policy details from new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, while weak economic data dimmed bets on higher interest rates.

item.title: Spain Is Set to Back BIS’s De Cos for ECB Helm, Expansion Says
item.description: The Spanish government plans to back Pablo Hernández de Cos as its candidate for the presidency of the European Central Bank, Expansión reported.

item.title: London Stock Exchange to Introduce Nonstop Trading Next Year
item.description: The London Stock Exchange will open a new venue outside of its regular market hours, a move to offer “near-continuous trading” and better compete with the 24/7 trading espoused by crypto platforms.

item.title: Indonesia Markets First Panda Bonds as It Broadens Funding
item.description: Indonesia has begun marketing its inaugural yuan-denominated bonds in China’s domestic debt market, as Southeast Asia’s largest economy seeks to diversify funding sources amid currency volatility and fiscal challenges.

item.title: Iran War Forces Cash-Strapped Asian Nations to Buy Expensive LNG
item.description: Pakistan and Bangladesh were forced to buy some of their most expensive liquefied natural gas shipments in years as the Middle East conflict chokes supply, straining government finances and prompting both countries to rethink their reliance on the super-chilled fuel.

item.title: Another Tanker Hit in Hormuz as Houthis Add to Regional Risks
item.description: Another tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as renewed hostilities empty the waterway, while a threat by Houthi rebels to blockade Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea heightened regional maritime risks.
